rows.claim: With no timings file, every shard keeps the split Playwright makes without the reporter.

facts.logLine: shard 1/3: no timings file at <tmp>/config-1/shard-timings.json; using Playwright's built-in sharding

rows.finding: Three shards with the reporter and no timings file ran the same leaves per shard as the same shards without the reporter (same split: true). Every record says `builtin` and names the missing file, and each shard logs it.

rows.claim: Two shards planned from the native records run every leaf once, and `check` passes.
rows.finding: One worker per shard, 52 of 52 tests known. Shards took 14193 / 14180 ms against 14007 / 14026 ms native, slowest 14193 ms against 14026 ms; harness violations none, `check` exit 0. A second native run of the same split had its slowest shard at 13989 ms.

rows.claim: Three shards planned from the native records run every leaf once, `check` passes, and the slowest shard is faster than under native sharding.
rows.finding: One worker per shard, 52 of 52 tests known. Shards took 9764 / 9775 / 9332 ms against 12412 / 3897 / 12511 ms native, slowest 9775 ms against 12511 ms; harness violations none, `check` exit 0. A second native run of the same split had its slowest shard at 12511 ms.

rows.claim: Under `--repeat-each 2` every shard balances, every copy runs once and `check` counts each copy apart.
rows.finding: Three shards, `--repeat-each 2`: harness violations none; `check` counted 104 distinct tests and exited 0, because a repeat carries its own suffix in the record.

rows.claim: Under `fullyParallel` the plan splits by test, keeps every serial group whole and runs every leaf once.
rows.finding: `fullyParallel`, three shards, one worker: harness violations none, records say granularity `auto`, slowest shard 9744 ms against 12480 ms native.

rows.claim: With `granularity: file` every spec file stays on one shard, also under `fullyParallel`; that grouping reads no `_parallelMode`, while the reporter still reads `_locks`.
rows.finding: `fullyParallel` with `granularity: file`, three shards: 0 files split across shards, harness violations none, slowest shard 9775 ms.

rows.claim: A renamed test and a new file run, and the plan counts them as unknown.
rows.finding: One test renamed and a new file of two tests, in both browser projects: every leaf ran once, and the plan line says 50/56 tests known, so 6 are priced by estimate.

rows.claim: Each balanced shard logs one line with its files, tests, estimate, the range of all shards, the timings sha and the plan sha.

facts.example: shard 1/3: 1 files, 5 tests, ~9.1s (all shards 7.4s-9.1s, largest group 9.0s), timings f1975ccd6896, 52/52 tests known, 1 worker(s), plan 0a1cdfe846e3

rows.finding: Every shard printed 1 line, all with timings `f1975ccd6896` and plan `0a1cdfe846e3`, for example: `shard 1/3: 1 files, 5 tests, ~9.1s (all shards 7.4s-9.1s, largest group 9.0s), timings f1975ccd6896, 52/52 tests known, 1 worker(s), plan 0a1cdfe846e3`.

rows.claim: Only the shards that host a test needing setup run it, and the predicted time of exactly those shards includes the setup cost.
rows.finding: Only `chromium` depends on setup, three shards: the shards that ran setup (1) are exactly the shards that host a `chromium` test. Each predicted time equals its work plus 106 ms of setup and teardown on those shards and its work alone on the others (true); harness violations none.

rows.claim: Under `--repeat-each` a test whose title reads like a repeat of another keeps its own identity in the records.
rows.finding: Tests `target` and `target (repeat 1)` under `--repeat-each=2`: the harness counts 8 leaves run once (violations none), while `check` exits 1, counts 6 distinct tests and reports `target (repeat 1)` as run twice (true), because a repeat is the key plus a ` (repeat N)` suffix.

rows.claim: Shards that read byte-identical copies of the timings file compute the same plan.
rows.finding: Three shards, each reading its own copy of the same bytes, logged plan `0a1cdfe846e3`, the plan of the run that shared one file; harness violations none.

rows.claim: The plan does not depend on Playwright's `--workers`: the reporter packs for its own `workers` option.
rows.finding: `--list` of the three shards with `--workers=1` and with `--workers=4` logged plan `0a1cdfe846e3`.

rows.claim: With a clock that jumps a second on every read, every shard computes the same plan as without it.
rows.finding: With a clock that runs one second ahead on every read, the three shards logged plan `0a1cdfe846e3`, against `0a1cdfe846e3` without it.

rows.claim: With strict off, a shard that cannot read its timings never splits the suite differently from the other shards.
rows.finding: Shard 2 read a truncated copy and fell back to the built-in split while shards 1 and 3 balanced (balanced, builtin, balanced). Every shard exited 0 and the harness found missing 5, duplicate 17, serial-split 2. `check` exits 1 and names the mixed split, after the tests ran.

rows.claim: With strict on, a shard that cannot read its timings fails before any test runs.

facts.message: playwright-shard-balancer: shard 2/3: cannot read timings: timings.json is not valid JSON: Unterminated string in JSON at position 3343 (line 165 column 7); strict mode stops the run rather than split it differently from other shards

rows.finding: Strict on, shard 2 reads a truncated copy: it exits 1 before any test, with an error that names the file and says strict mode stopped the run. Shards 1 and 3 exit 0 and 0, and no test runs twice. The run is red.

rows.claim: With strict on, an empty or absent timings file fails every shard before any test, so a first run must keep strict off.

facts.emptyMessage: playwright-shard-balancer: shard 1/2: timings file timings.json has no entries; strict mode stops the run rather than split it differently from other shards

rows.finding: Strict on with an empty timings file every shard exits 1 / 1, and with no file 1 / 1, before any test, each with an error that says the file has no entries or is missing. The restore action turns strict on only when the pinned file has entries for this reason.

rows.claim: `check` fails a run whose shards planned from different timings, naming the timings and the plan.
rows.finding: Shard 2 read a valid file in which the cart tests take twenty times as long. The shards exited 0 / 0 / 0 and the harness found duplicate 18, serial-split 2; `check` exits 1 and names different timings (true) and different plans (true).

rows.claim: `check` fails a run in which one shard ran without the reporter.
rows.finding: `--reporter=list` on shard 2 replaced the config's reporters, so that shard split natively and wrote no record. The shards exited 0 / 0 / 0 with missing 5, duplicate 17, serial-split 2; `check` exits 1 with `missing records for shard 2`.

rows.claim: When every shard runs without the reporter, the step after the shards cannot pass.
rows.finding: `--reporter=list` on both shards ran Playwright's own split (harness violations: none) and wrote no record. The shell lines of the finish action's `update` step, run with bash against the empty records folder, exit 1 with `::error::no run records`. `check` with no record exits 2, a usage error (true).

rows.claim: `check` fails when the record of a shard is missing.

problems: the shards ran 26 distinct tests, but each saw 52 before the split; pass --list to name the missing ones

rows.finding: The record of shard 1 alone: exit 1, `missing records for shard 2`.

rows.claim: `check` fails when a shard has two records, and counts every test of that shard as run twice.
rows.finding: Shard 1's record given twice: exit 1, `more than one record for shard 1`, 26 tests counted twice, the 26 tests of that shard.

rows.claim: `check` fails a run stopped by `--max-failures` and counts the tests that did not run.
rows.finding: A test that fails first and `--max-failures=1`: the shards exited 1 / 1 and both wrote a record; `check` exits 1 with 34 tests that did not run.

rows.claim: `check` fails a run whose shards saw different test sets before the split.
rows.finding: `--grep=cart` on shard 2 only: the records hold corpora of 52 and 6 tests, the harness found missing 26, duplicate 3, and `check` exits 1 naming the different test sets.

rows.claim: `check --summary` writes a table of predicted against measured time for every shard.

facts.heading: ### Shard balance: ok
facts.header: | Shard | Tests | Predicted | Test time | Whole run | Status |

rows.finding: Three shards: the summary starts `### Shard balance: ok` and has 3 shard rows under `| Shard | Tests | Predicted | Test time | Whole run | Status |`.

rows.claim: A failed run adds no sample, however long the failure took.
rows.finding: The volatile test failed after 3000 ms on each of its attempts (9099 ms in chromium, outcome `unexpected`). After `update` its samples are 1038 ms in chromium and 1046 ms in firefox, as before.

rows.claim: A cancelled run adds no sample for the interrupted test.
rows.finding: SIGINT 300 ms into the test: exit 130, the record says `interrupted` and marks the test as not run, and `update` leaves its samples at 1038 ms in chromium. Across the whole history `update` changed 1 entry, from the tests that passed before the signal.

rows.claim: From a full window, the price of a test that got faster follows it in three runs.
rows.finding: The volatile test went from about one second to 100 ms, starting from a window of five samples. Its chromium price before and after each of 3 faster runs: 1038 then 1038 then 1038 then 127 ms (samples 1038, 1038, 126, 127, 126). The median of the last five drops once the fast samples are the majority.

rows.claim: A flaky result adds one sample with every attempt summed, so a slow failed attempt inflates it, and the median of a full window absorbs one such sample.
rows.finding: The first attempt failed after 3000 ms and the retry passed in 1003 ms; the record gives one sample of 4008 ms. From the one-sample history the chromium price moves from 1038 to 2523 ms; from a full window it stays at 1038 ms.

rows.claim: A complete run in which one test failed leaves the history as it was.
rows.finding: The volatile test failed in a complete two-shard run (records failed, failed). `check` exits 0, since no test is missing, repeated or stopped, and `update` exits 0 and changes 54 entries of the history with the samples of the tests that passed; the failed test keeps its samples (true).

rows.claim: Passing samples of zero milliseconds never move the price of a full window to zero.
rows.finding: Three records in which the test passed in 0 ms, merged into a full window priced at 1038 ms: `update` accepts each (exit 0 / 0 / 0), the window holds 1038, 1038, 0, 0, 0 ms and the price is 0 ms.

rows.claim: `update` with a damaged history file or a damaged input exits non-zero and leaves the history as it was.

facts.stringSamplesMessage: timings.json has an invalid entry for "[chromium] › account.spec.js › account › loads the page"

rows.finding: A truncated history exits 1, a truncated record exits 1, and samples stored as text exit 1 (`timings.json has an invalid entry for "[chromium] › account.spec.js › account › loads the page"`); each history file keeps its bytes.

rows.claim: `update` skips an input it already merged, by the sha of its bytes.
rows.finding: The same record merged twice: the second `update` skipped 1 input with `already merged, skipped`, added 0 samples and left the file byte for byte as it was.

rows.claim: `update` from a filtered run keeps the entries of the tests the run left out.
rows.finding: After a `--grep=cart` run the history has 54 entries, as before (54). The 8 entries the run sampled gained a sample (a cart test now has 2) and every other entry kept its bytes. The cart test has its own entry in each browser project (true).

rows.claim: An entry no update has seen for more than 30 days is dropped, so a test filtered out for a month loses its history.
rows.finding: A `--grep=cart` update 30 days after the history was written keeps 54 of 54 entries; 31 days after, 8 are left, the tests that run sampled.

rows.claim: A setup test every shard ran gives one sample per update.
rows.finding: Both shards of the native run ran the setup project (2 records), and the history built from them holds 1 sample for it.

rows.claim: `update` refuses the records of fewer shards than ran.
rows.finding: The record of one of 2 shards: `update` exits 0, merges 28 samples and prints 0 warnings. The finish action runs `update` before `check` and saves when `update` succeeds.

rows.claim: The same inputs in the same order give the same bytes and sha with sorted keys; another order changes only the order of the `applied` list.
rows.finding: Two copies updated with the shard records in one order give `825ad83aad1d` and `825ad83aad1d`; the opposite order gives `b58c2fddb90f`, with the same entries (true) and the input shas listed in the other order. A writer that sorts its inputs gets the same bytes every time.

rows.claim: Two runs racing to publish never lose the updates of either.
rows.finding: Runs 101 and 102 both restored the same history and the older run saved last. The next run restores `pwsb-timings-101-1`, the most recently created entry: against merging both runs in sequence it lacks a sample in 8 entries, and its `applied` list does not hold the newer run's records (false).

rows.claim: One writer that merges every run into the newest history keeps the updates of both runs, and a replayed run changes nothing.
rows.finding: The writer merged the newer run and then the older one into one history: a cart test holds 3 samples, one from the baseline and one from each run. Replaying the older run skipped 2 inputs and kept the bytes.

rows.claim: A new test is priced at the median of its describe, else its file, else its project, else the whole suite, and a test skipped before it runs costs nothing.

new loose test in a known file
new file in a known project

rows.finding: On a suite with two describes and a loose test in one file, a second file and slower firefox tests, the four medians differ (true). The package's estimator gives 103 ms (known), 123 ms (describe), 402 ms (file), 142 ms (project), 673 ms (suite); our own medians give the same (true). A static skip costs 0 ms.

rows.claim: Under `--workers=2` the plan packed for one worker and the plan packed for two predict different shard times, and each predicts its shards within 25% on average.
rows.finding: Three shards under `--workers=2`: the plan for one worker predicted 9126 / 9119 / 7380 ms and missed the measured 9574 / 9541 / 5090 ms by 18.0% on average; the plan for two workers predicted 9126 / 9119 / 3858 ms against 9569 / 9566 / 5115 ms, off by 11.3%.

rows.claim: `simulate` predicts the slowest shard of the fixture within 25%, with the built-in split and balanced, and never predicts the balanced plan above the built-in split.
rows.finding: 2 shards: built-in 12763 ms simulated against 13802 ms measured, balanced 12760 ms against 14002 ms. 3 shards: built-in 11451 ms simulated against 12319 ms measured, balanced 9126 ms against 9579 ms. The balanced prediction is at or below the built-in one at every shard count (true).

rows.claim: `--overhead` adds a fixed cost per shard: once to the elapsed time and once per shard to the machine time, leaving the plan alone.
rows.finding: Three shards with `--overhead 90s`: elapsed 9126 ms becomes 99126 ms and machine time 25625 ms becomes 295625 ms; the balanced slowest shard stays 9126 ms.

rows.claim: `simulate` over a list and timings built from the S5 runs models couture-cast's measured two-shard split within 20%, and at no shard count predicts the balanced plan above the built-in split.
rows.finding: From 5 runs of `baseline-b` (160 tests): the built-in split of two shards simulates at 76620 ms against a measured median slowest shard of 77448 ms in tests, and balancing at 53553 ms against the S5 bound of 54609 ms. The per-shard overhead outside the Playwright run is 368 s median (353 to 464 s). No shard count predicts balancing above the built-in split (true).

rows.claim: Playwright marks every test inside a serial describe with a public `serial` annotation that carries the location of the describe.
rows.finding: 18 tests carry the annotation, the same tests the harness counts as serial (18), each with the location of its describe.

rows.claim: `describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' })` and `mode: 'default'` leave no trace in the public reporter API; only the internal `_parallelMode` differs.
rows.finding: The 8 checkout tests with `mode: 'parallel'`, with `mode: 'default'` and with no mode have the same public view (true); the file suite's `_parallelMode` is `parallel`, `default` and `none`.

rows.claim: A test lock leaves no trace in the public reporter API; only the internal `_locks` differs.
rows.finding: The 14 tests with and without `{ lock: 'database' }` have the same public view (true); `_locks` is set on 4 tests in one and 0 in the other.

rows.claim: Playwright's own sharding puts tests that share a lock on different shards, so a lock holds only inside one shard.
rows.finding: Two native shards of a suite whose four tests across two files and two projects share one lock: the lock tests ran on shards 1 and 2.

rows.claim: The reporter keeps every test that shares a lock on one shard.

notes: 3 group(s) joined to others that share a lock

rows.finding: Balanced over two shards, the lock tests ran on shard 1 only, and the plan line says `3 group(s) joined to others that share a lock`.

notes: lock information not found so tests that share a lock may run on different shards
